key_insight: The paper shows that AMR cell-density patterns can act as a compact latent representation for learning transient liquid–gas interface breakup across nozzle geometries.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster spray-nozzle design exploration by replacing expensive VOF-AMR CFD runs with a geometry-conditioned surrogate that preserves key breakup dynamics.
method: Train on 797 Basilisk VOF-AMR nozzle simulations.
Encode the AMR cell-density field as the latent proxy for refinement structure.
Use a second-stage model to reconstruct density evolution, nozzle geometry, and other flow variables.
evidence_signal: On held-out simulations, the surrogate matches key interface dynamics and runs in 0.045 s per trajectory, over 6×10^4 faster than Basilisk CFD.
watch_item: Because the model relies on AMR refinement structure as the main signal, performance may degrade when extrapolating to nozzle designs or breakup regimes far outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Learning Interface Breakup: A Geometry-Conditioned Latent Surrogate for Spray Formation
